神经退行性疾病.title: Nanobody-guided proximity proteomics reveals conformationally encoded molecular neighborhoods of LRRK2
神经退行性疾病.abstract: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is a multidomain signaling protein implicated in Parkinson's disease whose activity is closely linked to conformational state. How these structural transitions shape the cellular molecular environment of LRRK2 remains poorly understood. Here, we combined nanobody-mediated conformational control with miniTurbo proximity proteomics to define molecular neighborhoods associated with inhibitory, neutral, and activating LRRK2 states. Structural modeling suggested that the activating nanobody Nb22 targets the WD40 domain and destabilizes interactions maintaining the autoinhibited conformation. Consistent with this model, activation was accompanied by ordered, reciprocal remodeling of the LRRK2 proximity proteome, with progressive enrichment of centrosomal, ciliary, and RAB/endolysosomal machinery and depletion of soluble cytosolic, proteostasis-associated and 14-3-3 proteins. Notably, the Nb22-associated proteome combined centrosomal and endolysosomal components previously linked to distinct LRRK2 signaling environments. These findings support a model in which conformational transitions reorganize the spatial molecular neighborhood of LRRK2 and thereby couple kinase state to distinct cellular signaling networks.

神经退行性疾病.title: Striatal lateral inhibition regulates abnormal movements in a mouse model of levodopa-induced dyskinesia
神经退行性疾病.abstract: Striatal medium spiny neurons (MSNs) integrate convergent cortical, thalamic, and dopaminergic inputs to shape motor output. In addition, MSNs form local inhibitory synaptic connections with one another. Striatal lateral inhibition may contribute to the regulation of motor output, but its role in pathological motor function remains incompletely understood. Disruptions in motor function characterize several movement disorders, including levodopa-induced dyskinesia (LID), a complication of Parkinsons disease (PD) therapy characterized by involuntary movements. Here, we identify chronic changes in the strength of striatal lateral inhibitory synapses in a mouse model of PD/LID. These synapses are also modulated by acute dopamine signaling. Chemogenetic suppression of lateral inhibition originating from dopamine D2 receptor-expressing MSNs lowers the threshold for the expression of involuntary movements in vivo. Together, these findings identify a contribution of striatal lateral inhibition to motor dysfunction and suggest a broader role for this microcircuit in regulating motor output.

神经退行性疾病.title: Estradiol enhances sensory-evoked dilation of cortical penetrating arterioles in a mouse model of menopause despite pre-existing metabolic dysfunction
神经退行性疾病.abstract: Estrogen loss during menopause is a risk factor for cardiometabolic and neurovascular dysfunction, cognitive decline, and Alzheimers disease. Rodent studies of menopause have shown neuroprotective effects of 17{beta}-estradiol (E2) treatment when administered within a critical period, though these benefits have not been fully demonstrated in clinical trials of hormone therapy. A proposed explanation for this mismatch is the "healthy cell bias," where estrogen is only beneficial when initiated in physiologically intact systems. Our study investigates whether pre-existing metabolic dysfunction attenuates the effects of E2 on neurovascular coupling (NVC) in a rodent model of menopause. Female mice were fed 11 weeks of high-fat diet (HFD) or control diet (CD) to induce metabolic disease, followed by ovariectomy (OVX) and E2 or vehicle (Veh) treatment. NVC was assessed in awake mice using two-photon laser scanning microscopy of penetrating arterioles (PAs) in the somatosensory cortex, barrel field. Mice developed glucose intolerance and increased adiposity yet displayed intact NVC following HFD exposure, and subsequent OVX impaired NVC irrespective of metabolic health status. However, E2 treatment enhanced NVC responses regardless of diet relative to controls. These results indicate that estrogens effects on NVC are preserved in HFD+OVX conditions, which has implications for the use of hormone therapy in individuals that arrive at the menopause transition with pre-existing cardiometabolic disease.

神经退行性疾病.abstract: Background: Neuromelanin (NM) is a pigment that progressively accumulates with age in catecholaminergic neurons, particularly in the substantia nigra, ventral tegmental area, and locus coeruleus. These neuronal populations are especially vulnerable to degeneration in Parkinson s disease (PD). Elevated intracellular NM levels have been linked to neurodegeneration and PD-like phenotypes in experimental models. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying NM-induced pathology remain poorly understood, as human studies cannot disentangle the specific effects of NM accumulation from those of normal aging. Methods: We performed transcriptomic microarray analysis on laser-captured catecholaminergic neurons and regions (substantia nigra, ventral tegmental area, locus coeruleus) from NM-producing transgenic mice (tgNM) and NM-free wild-type controls across different ages, and compared them to data from postmortem human brain tissue. One of the molecular targets identified, GPNMB, was validated in mouse and human tissue, and functionally tested in vivo. Results: We identified region- and age-dependent transcriptional changes associated with progressive NM accumulation. NM consistently upregulated neuroinflammatory pathways with enrichment of disease-associated microglial genes, while downregulating transcription, translation, and mitochondrial functions. Locus coeruleus exhibited the earliest and strongest transcriptional alterations, whereas substantia nigra and ventral tegmental area showed a later-onset, age-progressive transcriptional dysfunction. Neuron-specific analyses revealed that many changes originated within NM-containing neurons rather than being solely glial-driven. NM-driven transcriptional profiles in mice strongly correlated with postmortem data from PD patients, underscoring their translational relevance. 神经退行性疾病.title: Linking Molecular Changes in the Hypothalamus to Alzheimer's Disease Phenotypes
神经退行性疾病.abstract: In many individuals with Alzheimer's disease (AD), sleep disruption and weight loss emerge years before the onset of memory decline and dementia. However, the cellular and molecular bases of these early events are not well understood. The hypothalamus is a critical brain region for the regulation of these behaviors, but its response to amyloid has not been systematically characterized. We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing to generate transcriptomic profiles of 1.1 million nuclei across the hypothalamus from 10 genetic backgrounds of the AD-BXD genetic reference panel spanning two ages and both sexes, including age-matched controls. Amyloid was associated with widespread, sex-biased molecular changes across diverse cell classes, including elevated neuroinflammatory signatures in microglia and astrocytes, upregulated ion transport pathways across barrier-associated cell types, and sex- and age-dependent changes to primary ciliary pathways in Glp1r+/Lepr+, Histaminergic, and Hcrt+ neuronal populations. Two metabolism-related populations showed differential expression exclusively in one sex: Glp1r+/Lepr+ neurons in females and Gpr50+ neurons in males. Several findings were conserved in analysis of human hypothalamus snRNAseq data, including reduced expression of TGF-{beta} pathway genes in medial mammillary body neurons and increased relative abundance of reactive Serpina3n+/YKL-40 astrocytes. This atlas provides a cellular framework for understanding the early, non-cognitive symptoms of AD and identifies several hypothalamic cell-type specific pathways that represent potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

神经退行性疾病.title: An Open, Evolving Brain and Cognitive Aging Simulator Enabled by Agentic Artificial Intelligence
神经退行性疾病.abstract: An agentic AI simulator was built to advance our understanding about how the human brain and cognition change with age. The simulator generates worlds based on hypothesized age-linked cascades and then simulates studies across varied experimental designs and selection criteria. Each simulated world begins with 120,000 individual lives initiated by baseline parameters (e.g., genetic risk, birth year) and then changed by age-dependent cascades (e.g., amyloid-dependent, cardiovascular). Examples illustrate how the simulator predicts distinct data patterns in cross-sectional versus longitudinal designs, how alternative participant selection strategies emphasize baseline differences versus age-related decline, and how variable levels of association emerge between brain and cognition dependent upon design choices. Simulations of clinical trials provide information about design, power, and outcome considerations. Experiments on alternative simulated worlds evaluate how well hypothesized cascades accommodate real-world data patterns, capturing the insights and open puzzles inside the application. Most critically, the application is built to evolve. Its code contains a complete description of how to construct and update itself so that any person or AI agent can explore a new finding, recalibrate to emerging data, or build and simulate a novel future study. The simulator is offered as a tool for understanding data patterns, teaching, and generation of hypotheses to be tested in future studies using real-world data collection.

神经退行性疾病.title: Neural mechanisms by which spaced learning promotes understanding
神经退行性疾病.abstract:
Spaced learning reliably improves memory. A few studies suggest it also benefits understanding and problem solving, but none has examined the neural mechanism. We hypothesised that this benefit arises because spacing changes the memory trace rather than merely strengthening it. To test this, we taught participants how unfamiliar words meanings could be derived from familiar parts: meaningful rather than rote learning. Each participant learned words in one session, or in two sessions about 2 h (massed) or 48 h (spaced) apart, to the same criterion; one-session words served as the reference. A common interval separated the last session from a delayed test with electroencephalography (EEG). Immediately after learning, self-rated understanding did not differ between schedules, yet under spacing participants revised more of their written test responses between sessions (35% versus 25%). At the delayed test, the spacing effect appeared: recognition was higher and self-rated explanatory retrieval more fluent after spaced than after massed learning. At the neural level, late-retrieval EEG patterns for remembered words were less similar to the reference after spaced than after massed learning, over right frontocentral and temporal sensors. In partly overlapping sensors and windows, lower similarity was statistically associated with a larger fluency advantage, suggesting that the change is directed rather than random. Behavioural evidence hinted at convergence across learners: between sessions, revisions under spacing were smaller and moved responses toward those of others. Together, these findings suggest that spacing changes the memory trace rather than merely strengthening it, in a direction linked to self-rated understanding.
